steps.text: Place the garlic, salt, lemon juice, vegetable oil, and olive oil in a quart-sized jar. Submerge an immersion blender in the mixture to the bottom of the jar. Mix with the blender resting on the bottom of the jar until the ingredients thicken, 1 to 2 minutes. Angle the mixer to pull ingredients from the sides of the jar and lift it toward the top to better combine. Continue blending until the mixture reaches a texture similar to mayonnaise.

raw_recipe.headline: Thick-Style Lebanese Garlic Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This sauce, using only garlic, salt, lemon juice, and oil, can be used as a condiment on grilled meats, as a salad dressing, and in dishes that require good garlic flavor.

review.reviewBody:
I have been making Lebanese Garlic Sauce for a few years, and this is the best recipe I have found. It tastes just like the sauce at our favorite Middle Eastern restaurant. I did make a few changes. Here is the recipe with my alterations:

 * 1 head garlic
 * 1/2 tablespoon sea salt (make sure it is course-ground or this will still be too much salt)
 * 1/2 cup fresh lemon juice
 * 1/2 cup vegetable oil
 * 3/4 cup olive oil (not extra virgin - mild-tasting, preferably cold-pressed)

So, less salt and less oil. Also, I believe the immersion blender is key here to emulsify the oil to the proper consistency. Loved it! Thank you for the recipe!

MMmm!! I love this stuff. I usually add a tablespoon of Mayonnaise that's the way I learned. For the reviewer that complained, -make sure your olive oil is a good quality, more $$ - and not stale- or else the taste will not be pleasant. Keep your oil in the coolest place, not a warm one. 
This is really yummy with roasted chicken- dip the pieces in and enjoy. Be careful or you will over-eat! Oh, and make sure the person who will be enjoying your close company later has had a good helping of it as well- or you will repel them. And stay home for a while.

I'm not sure how to rate this. I love garlic sauce and I only used the given ingredients but my amounts were completely different. I used twice as much garlic and only olive oil to make the consistency similar to what I grew up with. I loved what I made but it wasn't the recipe here.

Excellent recipe - I followed the directions exactly, although I did use less oil, as another reviewer suggested. I used 1 1/4 cups of canola-olive blend. I imagine using 2 cups of oil produces a sauce more like mayonnaise in consistency. We prefer the thicker type. I also reduced the amount of lemon juice and salt, but that was just for personal preference. 

You MUST use an immersion blender (hand blender / stick blender) and a narrow container (just wide enough for the blender blade), and place the blender blade at the bottom of the container at first. The action of the blade draws down and circulates the oil-garlic mixture. As the sauce thickens you can slowly raise the blender. The mixing container that came with the immersion blender was just the right size and shape, and I was amazed that the sauce started to thicken within seconds. And the final product - superb! The sauce held its form perfectly (did not separate) for the three days before it was all gone.

TL;DR: USE FRESH, HIGH QUALITY INGREDIENTS IN A NARROW CONTAINER AND ADD OIL IN A SLOW DRIZZLE WHILE BLENDER IS RUNNING FOR BEST RESULTS; WHEN DRIZZLED, YOU CAN USE YOUR COUNTERTOP BLENDER/FOOD PROCESSOR. EGG WHITE MAY HELP WITH GETTING RIGHT CONSISTENCY. I used this recipe as a springboard to make a garlic sauce to my liking. The result was very good, but I do feel it necessary to point out the following for those newer to cooking and/or making this for the first time: 

1. Garlic sauce is basically an emulsion of oil and lemon juice with garlic and salt in the mix. Because of this, I would suggest combining everything EXCEPT THE OIL in your mixing container, and then start mixing that with your blender. Then add the oil in a slow, constant drizzle while the blender is running so that you can optimize the emulsion; just dumping it all at once is not a good emulsion technique and may not get you the desired consistency. 

2. Quite a few reviewers suggested adding egg white, which makes sense considering mayonnaise (a condiment with similar texture and also an emulsion) uses eggs as part of the emulsion process. I added one egg white to my garlic sauce which may be the reason why I used much less oil than the recipe called for (about 2-3 fluid ounces). I should also note that I used the juice of one lemon which yielded about 1/4 cup of juice, and about 8-10 garlic cloves.

the ingredients are great and acurate but as a lebanese i would suggest blending the garlic with the salt first and then slowly adding the oil and the lemon in alternation as you blend. go slow and even though it's a little more complicated, if you do it right you'll end up with a really thick mixture almost like a sour cream dip! the process is a little tricky so even if it doesn't work the first time try again and make sure to keep an eye on the mixture as you blend so it wont fall appart. oh, and you might not need to use all of the oil and lemon, as soon as the mixture turns into a fluffy white substance and you think you have enought, taste it and if satisfied with the balance of flavors, you're done! :D

Excellent, love this sauce. It didn't thicken as I added all the ingredients slowly and alternating but I had added a little oil and lemon juice first to be able to blend the garlic and salt. Next time I will try to puree the garlic with the salt and THEN start adding the liquids alternating. I used a little egg white and it did thicken. Also my mistake was making it in a wider bowl as opposed to a tall thin jar. I should have read all the reviews first before making it. However after adding the egg white and transferring to a tall jar it blended and thickened wonderfully. The taste is 5 star, the recipe is 4 since you have to read the reviews to get the recipe to thicken right.

Oh my goodness this was SO good! I ran the wand mixer with the salt and garlic first, and then slowly added the oils and lemon juice to taste. I too was worried about how thin it was, and did end up putting an egg white in it. But after I did that, it was still thin. So then I saw another reviewer said to take the wand out and let it cool down. I did that, and put about 1/8 cup of remaining squeezed lemon juice (because I was adding to taste) in the fridge, and then added the chilled lemon juice into the mixing cup and did a quick mixer run right before serving, and it thickened up like a champ. Doing this you probably won't need the egg white. I didn't have non-EVOO, so I used half EVOO and half Canola oil, and it was absolutely fine. My husband is sitting here after dinner thinking of all the things he wants to make to lather that sauce all over. Just SPECTACULAR!!! Follow these tips and it'll be perfect.

FINALLY! A recipe for "garlic sauce" or "toum" that actually worked for me!

I used only canola oil (no olive oil), kosher salt, 8 cloves minced garlic, and the juice of one lemon.

I started by blending (with my immersion blender) the garlic, kosher salt and about 1/4 cup of the oil, just so I knew all the 'chucks' were broken up. After that I added the lemon juice and the rest of the olive oil. I blended with my immersion blender for almost 5 minutes and it was still soupy so I started experimenting. I added one egg white (helped a little) then I added 1T of ice water.. (HELPED A A LOT) the change was almost instantly thick white 'mayo'.

I will make a slight amendment that will make this sauce a bit thick:
1 head garlic, minced
1/2 a lemon juice (not 1/2 cup)
1 cup of oil (I use vegetable not olive)
1 teaspoon white vinegar
1 teaspoon mustard
1 egg white

Procedure: (you can use a regular blender or immersion blender, I prefer the immersion blender)

mince the garlic and place in the mixer bowl along with all ingredients except the oil
mix the above for 20 to 30 seconds
here is the trick:
start by adding the oil very very very slowly while continuing to mix, the oil should be added in a very thin line (not the whole amount) 
continue mixing and adding oil VERY slowly until the sauce becomes thick. usually it takes few minutes.

This is the best garlic sauce, and its used in restaurants.

I made this following Najib's variation, but I modified it slightly. I substituted 5 tbsp lemon juice in place if half lemon and 5 tsp garlic for a head of garlic and reduced salt from a TBSP to 1/2 TBSP. I also don't currently own an immersion blender, so I used a regular stand up type. You use what you have, right? I'm making shish tawook tonight and wanted to try this as recommended by other cooks. It turned out fantastic! Thick and garlicky. Delicious.

Thickened nicely. I blended for four minutes. It is pretty good but next time I may try reducing the lemon a bit. But if I use too little lemon I am worried that it might not emulsify. My garlic heads were very small so I used three.

For those of you have tried the recipe and felt betrayed by the inability to get the consistency right - DON'T DESPAIR. I have had inconsistent results of getting it to emulsify properly. I had all ingredients at room temperature, measured quantities according to recipe, and kept the immersion blender on high for several minutes. Yes - it mixed well, but remained liquidy. I left the kitchen for about an hour and was about to throw it out and start over. Not wanting to give up, I tried the immersion blender on the mixture again. Wow! it worked and gave me the consistency we were looking for. So, let it sit for a while after first try and try blending an hour later...
I tried to make this 3 times and I never turned out.

I didn’t have normal olive oil so I used 1.5cups canola oil + 0.5 EVOO. Still turned out great! I also added an extra head of garlic cos I like it spicy. Thank you for the emersion blender trick - this is the first time I’ve been successful (tried to use a food processor previously).
Great recipe but too watery for me, I did add more garlic and the egg white and it turned out perfect!

Flawless recipe. Tastes *exactly* like the toum I get in my favorite restaurant (7 hour drive away, different country, only get there once every few years!!)

If you're keto, this is a GENIUS way to get extra fat in your diet. I slather it on EVERYTHING. Throw a head of red cabbage in the food processor, combine a batch of this toum with it, and you have coleslaw for the entire week (its incredible). 

Be warned, you will smell of garlic, despite brushing your teeth and using listerine! I recommend having your friends/companions eat some too so they don't notice it :)
Super simple and amazingly delicious. Didnt modify anything. Its perfect. I licked the blender (dont judge me!!)
